content:
You write the short text of a strength-training app's weekly report. The app already shows every number, chart and the reason under each piece of advice; you add two things.

Period: 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-04 (one week, 7 days).
Status, decided by code: progressing (main lifts: 5 up, 0 flat, 0 down).
Sessions: 4 of 6 planned. Sets: 41 (last week 66).
Main lifts, best set this week:
- 深蹲: 100kg x 6 (last week 97.5kg x 6), up 2.6%
- 槓鈴臥推: 80kg x 8 (last week 77.5kg x 8), up 3.2%
- 槓鈴划船: 70kg x 8 (last week 67.5kg x 8), up 3.7%
- 羅馬尼亞硬舉: 90kg x 8 (last week 87.5kg x 8), up 2.9%
- 肩推: 45kg x 8 (last week 42.5kg x 8), up 5.9%
New records: 深蹲 100kg x 6; 槓鈴臥推 80kg x 8; 槓鈴划船 70kg x 8; 羅馬尼亞硬舉 90kg x 8; 肩推 45kg x 8.
Sets per muscle per week (range 10-20 for chest, back, legs, shoulders, glutes): chest 7, shoulders 7, triceps 2, back 7, biceps 2, legs 16.
No body weight logged.
The user's goal: "維持體能".
The user's note for this week: "這週出差，只練了四次".
Rules that fired. Advise only on these, by id:
- id "missed_sessions:-", priority 40, data {"done":4,"planned":6,"missed":2,"routines":"推日, 拉日","dates":"2026-10-01, 2026-10-03","lowGroups":"chest, shoulders, back"}. Advice: Name the missed sessions and suggest a realistic way to fit the work in or plan around those days. Never scold; if the note explains it, acknowledge that.

1. headline: one sentence the user reads first, the most important thing about this week, consistent with the status. It may use a number from above. At most 40 characters.
2. items: advice for at most 3 of the fired rules, most important first: usually by priority, but the goal or the note may change the order. A deload, if it fired, is always included and first. Each action is one or two short sentences saying exactly what to do next week, with the exercise, sets, weights or reps from the data. Don't repeat the reason; the app shows it.

Use only the numbers above; never invent data. No myths, no diagnosis, no scolding. Plain text only: no Markdown, no lists inside a field. Write in Traditional Chinese (繁體中文, Taiwan usage) with full-width punctuation (，。！？「」), and use the Chinese exercise names given above.
